title: Overview: the big ideas
summary: The chapter's key concepts and how its sections fit together.

blocks.md: Welcome to **Context Engineering** (Vol III). This overview gives you the chapter's big ideas before the section-by-section lessons. Read the claims once, flip the flashcards, then take the warm-up quiz: it is fine to miss questions here, the lessons that follow fill the gaps.

An agent's context window is a finite and expensive resource, not an unbounded repository for raw text. Naively accumulating tool outputs, conversational turns, and retrieved snippets exhausts token capacity, inflates prefill latency, and spreads attention across material the next decision does not need. Fitting is not the same as being usable.

rows: Before each call the runtime selects a bounded working set and splits the input allowance S_max - K_max among instructions, tool declarations, task state, and observations, and appended observations are the term that grows and displaces task state.

Usable context is an empirical property of a model, configuration, representation, and workload found by decision-level evaluation, because attention dilutes a target key as staged keys accumulate and position matters.

Staging the request as root, trunk, and leaf by change rate keeps the longest exact token prefix reusable, so volatile fields belong in the leaf, although correctness always overrides cache economics.
An observation is evidence only for the artifact versions and execution conditions under which it was gathered, and provenance labels on untrusted spans guide interpretation but enforce nothing.
Every compaction is a lossy transform that can silently drop evidence a later decision needs, so the runtime pins a protected-field set and keeps handles to raw records.

A model-written continuation record is an untrusted candidate that a host-side audit checks against a runtime-owned field inventory, the event log, and the workspace version before it replaces history.
A verified write withdraws current-state authority from bound observations and flags dependent conclusions for reassessment, without erasing their historical truth.

Context policies are compared as complete policies on accepted outcomes under a fixed model, tools, budget, and fixture, and retention or compression ratios are diagnostics with explicit denominators, not verdicts.
Separating a trigger watermark from a post-compaction target sets compaction cadence, and the amortized pass cost is judged against cost per accepted task, not local turn cost.
